title: Pramanik's Eight Wickets Put Bengal Six Wickets From Third Straight Ranji Win
excerpt: Left-arm spinner Pradipta Pramanik took four wickets in each innings as Bengal bowled Kerala out for 141, set a target of 409 and reduced the hosts to 53 for 4 by the close of day three in Thiruvananthapuram.
body:
• Bengal need six wickets on the final day to beat Kerala and record a third straight Ranji Trophy win this season.
  • Left-arm spinner Pradipta Pramanik took 4 for 44 in Kerala's first innings of 141 and 4 for 21 as the hosts slumped to 53 for 4 chasing 409.
  • Mohammed Shami took three first-innings wickets and Shahbaz Ahmed scored 121 in Bengal's first-innings 350.
  • Kerala captain Vishnu Vinod was unbeaten on 19 at stumps, with the hosts still needing 355 runs.

Bengal stand six wickets from a third consecutive Ranji Trophy victory after left-arm spinner Pradipta Pramanik dismantled Kerala for the second time in the match on day three at Mangalapuram in Thiruvananthapuram. Kerala, resuming on 101 for 6, were bowled out for 141. Bengal then made 198 in their second innings to set a target of 409, and Pramanik struck four more times before stumps to leave the hosts at 53 for 4.

Pramanik and Shami run through Kerala

Pramanik provided the breakthrough on the third morning, removing the experienced Jalaj Saxena for 6, caught by Sudip Gharami. He finished with 4 for 44 from 16.3 overs as Kerala's first innings folded for 141 in 51.3 overs. Mohammed Shami took three wickets and Shahbaz Ahmed two, completing a bowling performance that secured Bengal a first-innings lead of 209 runs. Bengal's 350 had been built on Shahbaz's 121 off 203 balls, a seventh-wicket recovery with Sumanta Gupta, who made 49, after the innings had slipped to 172 for 6. Ankur Paul top-scored among the openers with 66, while Kerala spinner Aditya Sarwate took four wickets.

Saxena fights back, but the target stays out of reach

Kerala's bowlers kept the match alive in Bengal's second innings. Saxena, the veteran off-spinner, took 5 for 70 in 18 overs as Bengal were dismissed for 198 in 46 overs. Abhimanyu Easwaran top-scored with 47, Sudip Chatterjee made 34 and Shami added a useful 29 at number ten. Openers Easwaran and Paul had added 46 for the first wicket before Nedumankuzhy Basil removed Paul for 12. The collapse, however, only trimmed Bengal's advantage rather than threatening it: the 209-run lead meant Kerala still faced a target of 409 on a wearing pitch.

"Bengal need six wickets on the final day to beat Kerala and record a third straight Ranji Trophy win this season."

A second collapse ends Kerala's realistic hopes

Chasing 409, Kerala's top order faltered again, and again it was Pramanik who did the damage. He removed Abhishek Nair leg-before without scoring, had Saxena — opening the innings — caught by Chatterjee for 18, bowled the other Abhishek Nair for a duck and had Sachin Baby stumped for 10, at which point Kerala were 51 for 4. Pramanik's second-innings spell read 10-2-21-4 by the close. Captain Vishnu Vinod was unbeaten on 19, with Salman Nazir yet to score, and Kerala need 355 more runs on the final day with six wickets in hand.

What it means

For Bengal, a win would make it three victories in a row this Ranji season and strengthen their position in the group. The match has also underlined the value of their spin depth: between them, Pramanik and Shahbaz have controlled the game on a surface offering turn, while Shami's three first-innings wickets continued his productive return to competitive cricket. Kerala, by contrast, face a final day built around survival. Vinod is the last recognised batter with form in the match, and the hosts' realistic target now is to bat out the day rather than chase 409.

What's next

Play resumes on the fourth and final day with Kerala at 53 for 4. Bengal need six wickets to complete the win; Kerala need to survive the day to salvage a draw.
